last month agents settled $24 million across 75 million x402 payments, an average of 32 cents per transaction. @Visa moves that much in under a minute, and it still took a premier seat in the x402 foundation this month, alongside @Mastercard, @stripe, @Google, @awscloud, and @circle.

the transaction count explains the seat at the table. 75 million payments means software made 75 million independent decisions about what a resource was worth, then paid for it in a single http request.

@chainalysis found transactions above $1 grew from 49% of volume in early 2025 to 95% by early 2026. agents started with sub-cent api pings and graduated to buying compute, data, and services at real prices.

the networks that spent 50 years perfecting human checkout are now helping write the standard for machine checkout. every api, dataset, and model endpoint becomes a storefront the moment an agent can pay for it in one request.

we built ampersend for this market: discover an api on the marketplace, pay per call in USDC on @base, settle over x402 in seconds.

������ Ideathon — July 29

x402 just went institutional: 40-member Linux Foundation, Visa + Mastercard + Stripe onboard, cards joining stablecoins.

The standard won. The tooling around that new reality? Barely started.

3 things worth shipping this week ������������ https://t.co/22wUnXIhSa

3/ Card → 402 fallback ������

x402's roadmap adds cards next to stablecoins. But tons of agents still have zero crypto wallet.

Ship: a fiat fallback that catches the 402, settles from a card via an on-ramp, and completes the request.

Bring the non-crypto crowd onchain.

1/ The universal translator ������

x402 isn't alone — AP2, ACP & Visa's TAP all want the agent. But AP2 is built to *carry* x402 as a payment method.

Ship: an adapter that lets any AP2 / A2A agent pay your x402 endpoint natively.

One endpoint. Every agent can pay it.
